findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian translation of `totpStep1` was changed from Lithuanian to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Users with the Lithuanian locale will see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page of the account console. It should be a Lithuanian rendering of the new English source 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:' (e.g. starting with 'Įdiekite vieną iš šių programų...').

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian translation of `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the login OTP setup page. It should be translated from the new English source 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:' into Lithuanian.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file contains Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: In the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) message file, `totpStep1` was changed to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式, 裝) while the rest of the file is Simplified Chinese. Mainland China users will see mixed script. It should use Simplified characters, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

findings.title: Diff-trimming code can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: When a sanitized value differs from the original, the code trims common prefix (`start`) and common suffix (`end`) independently. If the common prefix and suffix overlap — i.e. start + end exceeds the length of one of the strings — then `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` or `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` is called with beginIndex > endIndex and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. For example value `helloaab` sanitized to `helloab` (or `ab` vs `aab`) yields start=6, end=2, so substring(6, 5) is invoked. This would crash the verifier with a confusing exception instead of reporting the illegal HTML. `end` should be capped, e.g. at min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws untyped RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
findings.body: verify() wraps IOErrors in MojoExecutionException with a clear message, but the newly added verifySafeHtml() re-opens the message file and the derived English file and throws RuntimeException on any IOException (e.g. a community translation whose computed English counterpart under `resources` does not exist). This aborts the Maven build with a raw RuntimeException stack trace rather than a proper mojo failure message, and is inconsistent with the error handling contract of verify(). These catches should throw MojoExecutionException (or add a clear violation message) instead.

findings.title: No test asserts a clean file produces zero violations
findings.body: All four tests only assert that a specific violation message is present (hasItem) in files crafted to be invalid. There is no test asserting that a valid translation (e.g. noHtml_en.properties, or a translation whose HTML exactly matches the English source) returns an empty message list. Since this verifier runs against every message file in the build, a false-positive bug in the sanitizer logic would fail the build for all locales and would not be caught by these tests. The switch from Matchers.contains to hasItem in verifyDuplicateKeysDetected also means extra unexpected messages no longer fail that test.
